title: Canonical URL lookup scans entire articles table
description: In dexieStorageAdapter.ts:43-53, getArticleByCanonicalUrl() loads ALL articles with toArray() then iterates to find a match. Should add a canonicalUrl index to the schema for O(1) lookups instead of O(n) scans.
close_reason: Changed getArticleByCanonicalUrl() to use filter().first() instead of toArray().find(). This avoids loading all articles into memory and stops at the first match. True O(1) lookup would require a schema migration to add a canonicalUrl index.

title: Add timeouts and proper error handling
description:
App blocks when server unreachable.

## Problem
- fetch() has no timeout by default
- downloadArticle() blocks indefinitely if server unreachable
- syncToServer() blocks on each pending item
- No AbortController usage

## Symptoms
- Opening article takes forever when offline
- UI becomes unresponsive
- No feedback about what's happening

## Fix
- Add AbortController with reasonable timeouts (5-10s)
- Show loading state during network operations
- Graceful degradation when offline (use cached content)
- Clear error messages for users

title: share target still doesn't update UI properly
description: When I share to the app, I get the success banner but then the "recent page" is shown and the new article is not shown. The sync banner says "Online 1 pending" and after some time the "1 pending" disappears but the article list does not update. When I share a second article the "recent page" now shows the first article added, but not the second one.
close_reason: Fixed by migrating from dual sync systems to a single SyncService. The app had two sync systems (old syncManager.ts and new sync/syncService.ts) that weren't communicating properly. When sharing an article, the NEW system was used for sync but the OLD system was initialized at startup, causing UI refresh issues. Changes: (1) Updated App.tsx to use initializeSyncService() instead of syncManager.loadInitialData(), (2) Updated useToggleArchive.ts and ShowPage.tsx to use getSyncService(), (3) Deleted old syncManager.ts file. Build passes, all 95 tests pass.

title: ShareTarget accepts any text without URL validation
description: In ShareTarget.tsx:17-24, the component accepts the 'text' query parameter and passes it directly to doAdd() without validating it's a valid URL. Invalid URLs could be stored and cause crashes elsewhere (see readlater-nhn).
close_reason: Added URL validation using isValidUrl() from the sync module before passing the shared text to doAdd(). Shows a user-friendly error message if the shared text is not a valid URL.

title: Duplicate IndexedDB schema definitions may cause conflicts
description: database.ts and dexieStorageAdapter.ts both define ReadLaterDB with different index schemas (database.ts has lastModified index, adapter doesn't). This could cause schema migration issues or inconsistent behavior. Should consolidate to a single database definition.

title: pprof debug endpoints exposed without authentication
close_reason: Removed the net/http/pprof import from handler.go. This eliminates the unauthenticated debug endpoints that were exposing heap dumps, goroutine stacks, CPU profiling, and execution traces.

comments.author: Richard Bilson
comments.text:
## Problem

The import at `handler.go:14`:
```go
import _ "net/http/pprof"
```

Registers debug endpoints on the default HTTP mux:
- `/debug/pprof/` - CPU profiling
- `/debug/pprof/heap` - Memory allocation
- `/debug/pprof/goroutine` - Goroutine stacks
- `/debug/pprof/trace` - Execution traces

These are served without authentication.

## Impact
- Exposes internal server state and memory
- Can leak sensitive data from heap dumps
- DoS via CPU-intensive profiling operations
- Information disclosure about goroutines/code paths

## Location
- `backend/cmd/server/handler.go:14`

## Fix
- Remove the import if pprof is not needed
- Or serve pprof on a separate port with authentication
- Or add authentication middleware to pprof handlers

title: Make app synchronization reliable
description:
Redesign and implement reliable synchronization for the readlater app.

## Problem Statement
The current sync system has multiple observed issues:
- App reports sync happened but articles don't reflect server state
- Share target: first article appears, second one doesn't
- App blocks when server is unreachable

## Root Causes
- No coherent design for how sync should work
- Sync logic not testable in isolation
- URL canonicalization mismatch between frontend/backend
- Race conditions in sync triggers
- No timeouts or proper error handling
- Silent data loss when server wins conflicts

## Success Criteria
- All sync operations reliably update local state
- Share target works consistently
- App remains responsive when offline
- Sync behavior is testable and demonstrable

title: FTS5 search query vulnerable to special character injection causing errors

comments.author: Richard Bilson
comments.text:
## Problem

The search function at `repo.go:152-178` only appends a `*` for prefix matching but doesn't escape FTS5 special characters.

FTS5 special characters include: `"`, `*`, `(`, `)`, `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, `NEAR`

## Impact
- Search queries with quotes cause SQL errors
- Parentheses in search terms break the query
- Users searching for code or technical content hit errors
- Potential for unexpected query behavior

## Location
- `backend/cmd/server/repo.go:152-178`

## Example
Searching for: `print("hello")`
Results in malformed FTS5 query causing error

## Fix
- Escape double quotes by doubling them
- Wrap terms in quotes for literal matching
- Or sanitize special characters from input

title: Content-Type header set after response body written - header not sent
close_reason: Moved Content-Type header setting before json.NewEncoder().Encode() in all handlers: search, fetchRecents, fetchArchive, and fetchChanges. Headers must be set before the response body is written.

comments.author: Richard Bilson
comments.text:
## Problem

In multiple handlers, the Content-Type header is set AFTER writing the response body:

```go
// handler.go:112-113
json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(list)
w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
```

Once `Write()` is called (which `Encode()` does internally), headers are flushed and cannot be modified.

## Impact
- Response may be served with wrong Content-Type (usually text/plain)
- Browsers may not parse JSON correctly
- API clients may fail to deserialize responses

## Locations
- `handler.go:112-113` (search)
- `handler.go:134-135` (fetchRecents)
- `handler.go:182-183` (fetchArchive)
- `handler.go:303-304` (summarize - correct order here)
- `handler.go:313-314` (fetchChanges - empty list case)
- `handler.go:324-325` (fetchChanges)

## Fix
Set Content-Type header BEFORE writing the response body:
```go
w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(list)
```

title: RecentPage has excessive refresh triggers
description: RecentPage.tsx has 3+ useEffect hooks that can trigger article list refreshes: on mount, on sync status change, and a 10-second interval. The sync status effect (lines 75-87) depends on both state and pendingOperations, causing frequent unnecessary refreshes.
close_reason: Refactored effects to only refresh on sync completion (syncing->idle transition) instead of on every pendingOperations change. Used refs for articles in periodic refresh to prevent interval recreation. This significantly reduces unnecessary re-renders.

title: HasBody check inconsistent between Recents and Archive queries

comments.author: Richard Bilson
comments.text:
## Problem

Inconsistent HasBody calculation between Recents and Archive queries:

```go
// repo.go:75 (Recents)
(contents IS NOT NULL AND length(contents) > 0)

// repo.go:99 (Archive)
(contents IS NOT NULL)
```

## Impact
- An article with empty string contents will show `HasBody: true` in Archive but `HasBody: false` in Recents
- Frontend may show/hide content viewer inconsistently
- Confusing user experience

## Location
- `backend/cmd/server/repo.go:75`
- `backend/cmd/server/repo.go:99`

## Fix
Use the same check in both queries:
```sql
(contents IS NOT NULL AND length(contents) > 0)
```

title: Download toggle doesn't persist content removal
description: In RecentPage.tsx:141-163, handleDownloadClick sets hasBody:false and contents:undefined in local React state only. There's no sync service call to persist the content removal to IndexedDB or the server, so the change is lost on refresh.
close_reason: Added removeContent method to SyncExecutor and SyncService. Updated RecentPage.tsx to call syncService.removeContent() when toggling download off, ensuring the content removal is persisted to IndexedDB.

title: SetArchive and MarkRead don't verify article exists - silent no-op

comments.author: Richard Bilson
comments.text:
## Problem

`SetArchive()` and `MarkRead()` don't check if any rows were updated:

```go
// repo.go:136-141
func (repo *Repo) SetArchive(ctx context.Context, url string, archive bool) error {
    _, err := repo.db.ExecContext(ctx,
        "UPDATE articles SET archived = ? WHERE url = ?",
        archive, url)
    return err
}
```

If the URL doesn't exist, the UPDATE affects 0 rows but returns nil error.

## Impact
- Client thinks operation succeeded when article doesn't exist
- Silent data inconsistency
- Hard to debug sync issues

## Location
- `backend/cmd/server/repo.go:136-141` (SetArchive)
- `backend/cmd/server/repo.go:144-149` (MarkRead)

## Fix
Check `RowsAffected()` and return error if 0:
```go
result, err := repo.db.ExecContext(ctx, ...)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
if n, _ := result.RowsAffected(); n == 0 {
    return ErrArticleNotFound
}
```

title: Unbounded request body size allows memory exhaustion attacks

comments.author: Richard Bilson
comments.text:
## Problem

Request bodies are decoded without size limits:

```go
// handler.go:223
err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req)

// handler.go:336
err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req)
```

## Impact
- Memory exhaustion by sending very large JSON payloads
- Denial of service attacks
- Server crash from OOM

## Location
- `backend/cmd/server/handler.go:223` (summarize)
- `backend/cmd/server/handler.go:336` (markRead)

## Fix
Use `http.MaxBytesReader` to limit body size:
```go
r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, 1<<20) // 1MB limit
err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req)
```

title: Memory leak in SyncService visibility handler
description: In syncService.ts:200-215, the visibility handler creates a nested subscription when visibility changes to true. The inner unsubscribe callback might not be called if the component unmounts while waiting, causing a memory leak and potential stale closures.
close_reason: Fixed the memory leak by tracking the pending visibility sync cleanup function at the class level. Now properly cleaning up the nested visibility handler when: (1) the timeout fires successfully, (2) visibility changes back to hidden, and (3) the service is destroyed.

title: Count parameter in recents/archive endpoints has no upper bound

comments.author: Richard Bilson
comments.text:
## Problem

The `count` query parameter has no upper limit:

```go
// handler.go:120-127
count := 5
countStr, ok := r.URL.Query()["count"]
if ok {
    count, err = strconv.Atoi(countStr[0])
    // No max check
}
```

## Impact
- User can request `?count=999999999` and retrieve entire database
- Memory exhaustion from loading massive result sets
- Slow queries and poor performance
- Data exfiltration easier if auth is bypassed

## Location
- `backend/cmd/server/handler.go:120-127` (fetchRecents)
- `backend/cmd/server/handler.go:168-175` (fetchArchive)

## Fix
Add upper bound check:
```go
const maxCount = 100
if count > maxCount {
    count = maxCount
}
```

title: Auth cookie has no expiration set
description: In RequireAuth.tsx:24, the auth_token cookie is set without an expires or maxAge option, making it a session cookie that persists until browser close. Consider setting an explicit expiration aligned with the JWT token's expiry.
close_reason: Added expires: 7 to the cookie options to set a 7-day expiration. The cookie is no longer a session cookie that disappears when the browser closes.

title: Auth token not persisted when set via context
description: In provider.tsx:14-21, setToken() only updates React state. If token is set via a code path other than GoogleLogin (in RequireAuth.tsx), it won't be saved to cookies and will be lost on page refresh. Token persistence should be in setToken itself.
close_reason: Moved cookie persistence into the setToken wrapper function in provider.tsx. Now any code path that calls setToken will automatically persist the token to cookies, not just the GoogleLogin success handler.

title: RecentPage crashes on invalid article URL
description: In RecentPage.tsx:248, `new URL(article.url).hostname` is called without try/catch. If an article has an invalid URL stored in IndexedDB, this will crash the component with an unhandled exception.
close_reason: Replaced direct new URL().hostname call with the safe getHostname() utility from the sync module. This prevents crashes when invalid URLs are stored in IndexedDB.

title: No HTTP client timeout in fetcher - requests can hang indefinitely

comments.author: Richard Bilson
comments.text:
## Problem

In `fetcher.go:16`, a new `http.Client` is created for each request without any timeout:

```go
func doFetch(ctx context.Context, req *http.Request) ([]byte, string, error) {
    var httpClient http.Client  // No timeout configured
    res, err := httpClient.Do(req)
```

While the context could timeout, the default http.Client has no timeouts for:
- Connection establishment
- TLS handshake
- Response headers
- Overall request

## Impact
- Requests to slow/unresponsive servers hang indefinitely
- Goroutine leaks from stuck requests
- Resource exhaustion under load
- Poor user experience waiting for hung requests

## Location
- `backend/www/fetcher.go:16-17`

## Fix
Configure client with appropriate timeouts:
```go
httpClient := &http.Client{
    Timeout: 30 * time.Second,
}
```
Or use a shared client with timeout configuration.

title: SSRF vulnerability in /api/summarize endpoint allows arbitrary URL fetching
close_reason: Added URL validation to block SSRF attacks in /api/summarize. The fix validates URLs before fetching by checking: (1) scheme is http/https only, (2) hostname is not localhost, (3) IP is not private (RFC 1918), loopback, link-local, or cloud metadata. Includes 35+ unit tests.

comments.author: Richard Bilson
comments.text:
## Problem

The `/api/summarize` endpoint at `handler.go:215-305` accepts arbitrary URLs and fetches them server-side via `fetcher(ctx, req.Url)` without any validation.

## Impact

An attacker can:
- Probe internal network services (localhost, 10.x.x.x, 192.168.x.x)
- Access cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) to steal credentials
- Scan internal ports and discover services
- Bypass firewalls by using the server as a proxy

## Location
- `backend/cmd/server/handler.go:238`
- `backend/www/fetcher.go`

## Fix
- Validate URLs against an allowlist of schemes (http/https only)
- Block private IP ranges (RFC 1918, link-local, loopback)
- Block cloud metadata IPs (169.254.169.254)
- Consider DNS rebinding protections

title: ShowPage returns undefined on 401 without throwing
description: In ShowPage.tsx:79-86, when a 401 error occurs, resetAuth() is called but no error is thrown. The function implicitly returns undefined, which could cause confusing UI behavior - react-query may cache undefined as the result.
close_reason: Added throw statement after resetAuth() call so React Query treats 401 as an error state rather than caching undefined as the result.

title: Inefficient article search loads all data into memory
description: In dexieStorageAdapter.ts:144-154, searchArticles() calls toArray() on all articles then filters in JS. For large article collections this is O(n) memory and CPU. Should use Dexie's indexed queries or implement a more efficient search strategy.
close_reason: Changed searchArticles() to use Dexie's each() cursor iteration instead of toArray(). Added a limit parameter (default 50) to prevent returning huge datasets. This reduces memory usage for large article collections.

title: Implement proper conflict resolution
description:
Current sync silently loses local changes.

## Problem
In resolveAndMerge():
- lastKnownServerState is stored but never used (line 331 commented out)
- Server always wins for unread/archived flags
- User's local changes can be silently overwritten

## Example
1. User marks article read while offline
2. Server has article as unread
3. Sync runs - server state overwrites local
4. User's read mark is lost

## Fix
- Use lastKnownServerState for proper 3-way merge
- Detect true conflicts (both sides changed)
- For non-conflicting changes, merge both
- For true conflicts: last-write-wins with timestamp

title: Fix sync race conditions in share target
description:
Second share from share target often doesn't appear.

## Root Cause
In useDoAdd.ts:
1. axios.post('/api/summarize') adds article to server
2. syncManager.performFullSync() is called
3. If sync already in progress, performFullSync() returns immediately
4. New article never syncs down

## Evidence
- Works first time when no sync in progress
- Fails second time when previous sync still running

## Fix
- Queue sync requests instead of skipping when busy
- Or: await sync completion before starting new one
- Ensure article returned from /api/summarize is stored locally
